primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Disruption of advanced atherosclerotic plaques, often after aortic or arterial instrumentation, releases cholesterol crystals that lodge in small renal arteries and arterioles. Partial luminal obstruction plus a secondary inflammatory/giant-cell reaction causes subacute ischemic kidney injury; systemic microembolization can produce livedo reticularis or blue toes while distal pulses remain palpable.
vignette: A 72-year-old man with diffuse atherosclerotic disease undergoes coronary angiography. Ten days later, serum creatinine has progressively increased. He has painful blue discoloration of several toes despite palpable pedal pulses and a mottled reticular rash on both legs. Laboratory studies show peripheral eosinophilia and mildly decreased complement levels. Urinalysis shows only mild proteinuria and a few red blood cells.
lead: Which renal biopsy finding would most directly identify the cause of this patient’s kidney injury?
correct: Needle-shaped cholesterol clefts occluding small renal arteries and arterioles with surrounding inflammation
distractors: Diffuse acute tubular epithelial injury with loss of brush borders and granular casts but no vascular deposits
A fibrin-rich thrombus completely occluding a large main renal artery branch
Granular subendothelial immune-complex deposits along glomerular capillary loops
Polarizable calcium oxalate crystals obstructing tubular lumina
distractor_notes: Acute tubular injury can follow iodinated contrast exposure, but it does not explain the delayed systemic microembolic skin findings, eosinophilia, and small-vessel cholesterol-crystal lesions characteristic of atheroembolism.
A large thromboembolus to a main renal arterial branch causes a renal infarction pattern rather than diffuse cholesterol microembolization with blue toes and livedo while pulses remain present.
Immune-complex glomerulonephritis produces glomerular inflammatory findings and active urine sediment; it does not explain cholesterol embolization after vascular instrumentation.
Oxalate nephropathy produces intratubular calcium oxalate deposition and has a different metabolic or toxic exposure context.
key_expl: The delayed kidney injury after angiography together with blue toes, livedo reticularis, eosinophilia, and preserved distal pulses is classic for cholesterol crystal embolization. Instrumentation can disrupt an aortic atherosclerotic plaque, releasing cholesterol crystals that shower small arteries and arterioles in the kidneys and other organs. During tissue processing, cholesterol dissolves and leaves elongated needle-shaped or biconvex clefts within vessel lumina, often surrounded by an inflammatory and giant-cell reaction.
objective: Recognize atheroembolic renal disease as cholesterol crystal microembolization from disrupted atherosclerotic plaques and identify the characteristic small-vessel cholesterol clefts on biopsy.
